reuse.why: Extends the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds shared predicates (skipsWeekendDays, isSkippedWeekendDay, scan/shift bounds), but each consumer still assembles the full weekend rule itself instead of calling one shared 'apply weekend rule' function.

duplication.why: The composition 'skip if daily weekend/holiday, else move if skipWeekend, else keep' is written three times: applyWeekendRule in schedules/app.ts, getWeekendMovedDay plus an isSkippedWeekendDay guard in budget/schedule-template.ts, and inline in getNextDate/findNextOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts.

placement.why: Holiday and weekend predicates correctly live in shared/schedules.ts, but the full rule (applyWeekendRule) is private to server/schedules/app.ts and a near twin is private to schedule-template.ts, rather than in the shared module.

scope.why: Mostly what the four steps need; restricting getNextDate's reverse fallback to bounded schedules (isBoundedSchedule) is an extra behaviour tweak.

maintainability.why: Bounds and predicates are well commented, but a future weekend/holiday rule change must be repeated in three call-site compositions that can drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts getWeekendMovedDay and getNextDate's inline skipDays/getDateWithSkippedWeekend logic re-implement what applyWeekendRule in schedules/app.ts does, instead of sharing one function.

disguised_duplication.where: applyWeekendRule (app.ts), getWeekendMovedDay + isSkippedWeekendDay guard (schedule-template.ts) and findNextOccurrence filter + skipWeekend branch (getNextDate) are the same rule reshaped and renamed per site.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; the daily-skip special case is not taken by any shared function, so three call sites (schedules/app.ts applyWeekendRule, schedule-template.ts getWeekendMovedDay, shared getNextDate) each compose skipsWeekendDays/isSkippedWeekendDay with getDateWithSkippedWeekend themselves.
